text:
maya: heads up — noticed a smallbatch p95/p99 latency spike on canary after the host image update that included driver 12.14p1 + torch2.8. Small repro shows heavy KV-cache churn and selector jitter. CI flagged the smoke-smallbatch-latency job: https://ci.internal/reports/7732 :exclamation:

samir: can you paste the profiler traces? is this across models or one family?

maya: quick logs and flame snippet below from the failing canary (a100, 32seq workload). overall: p95 ~120ms -> 260ms, tail is noisy.

maya: ```
perf: request 2026-03-18T12:03:02Z model=gpt-medium seq=32 batch=1
kv_cache: evict_rate=0.38, prefetch_hit=0.21, prefetch_miss=0.79
selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_v2 (alternating with matmul_v1)
GPU util: 62% -> erratic spikes to 95%
latencies: p50=45ms p95=260ms p99=430ms
stack: runtime.autotune->selector->triton_dispatch->cublasLt
```

jonah: hmm selector alternating between v1 and v2 is a red flag — could be autotune table invalidated by a cuda/cudnn driver change. did the deploy include a triton or nvrtc bump?

maya: only driver + OS libs, no triton change. but torch2.8 landed in the image too. infra-bot: deployment 2026-03-18T11:58 completed (image: rwinf/runtime:2026-03-18-2)

ethan: CI job output: ``smoke-smallbatch-latency failed on canary-3 with 2.3x p95 regression``. stacktrace points to `dispatch_matmul_workspace` fallback code path.

samir: can you run a bisect against the image layers? start by swapping back to previous driver (12.13) kernel modules in canary nodes and retest. if revert not possible, try forcing selector to prefer matmul_v1 via selector_override for a micro-benchmark.

maya: started an A/B canary: group A pinned to driver12.13 (image: rwinf/runtime:2026-03-17-9), group B is current. early numbers: group A p95=118ms, group B p95=257ms. so repro looks driver-related.

li-chen: rolling back driver cluster-wide isn't feasible for enterprise tenants. short-term mitigation: force selector override to prefer the stable matmul path and increase kvcache capacity for smallbatch traces. also add a prefetch backoff to reduce thrash. can we patch runtime config and push a hotfix?

jonah: I'll take selector override + kvcache capacity change as hotfix. we'll also instrument a tighter metric on prefetch_miss and kernel_switch_rate. if that stabilizes we can do a minimal rollout while we bisect driver/Torch interplay.

maya: created PR with runtime config changes: rwinf/runtime#4893 — selector.prefer=matmul_v1, kvcache.lru_size=1.5x, prefetch.backoff_ms=8. kicking canary.

ethan: filing a CI ticket and scheduling a deeper bisect job to test driver vs torch layer. tagging infra: @samir @jonah to coordinate node-level driver swap automation. :calendar:

samir: quick note — add a deterministic unit test that asserts kernel selection stability for tiny-batch workloads so this doesn't regress silently in CI again.

infra-bot: canary rollout started: rwinf/runtime#4893 -> canary-3 (20% traffic)

maya: thanks. will monitor p95/p99 and KV metrics. if we see >1.5x tail after 30m we rollback the canary. :thumbsup:

jonah: filing follow-ups: bisect task, CI smallbatch smoke add, telemetry alert for kernel_switch_rate.

maya: summary of next steps in one line: hotfix config -> monitor -> bisect driver/torch -> durable fix in selector heuristics + regression test.
